name: MRPeasy
summary: Cloud manufacturing ERP for small manufacturers. Plan production, track inventory and manage orders and procurement so a growing workshop runs without spreadsheets.
best_for: small manufacturers, wholesalers and distributors who want dependable production planning and inventory control without a heavy ERP or a dedicated IT team
skip_if: you're a large or highly complex manufacturer, or you need deep customisation, advanced analytics and forecasting — MRPeasy is built for simplicity, not complexity
honest_knock: Paying ~$50 per user just so a shop-floor worker can clock in and out feels steep when they'll touch a fraction of the features. Customisation and reporting are limited and there's no advanced demand forecasting, so larger or highly complex manufacturers will outgrow it. The built-in AI assistant, Mr. Peasy, can read your data since 28 September 2026, but only after an admin switches that on, only read-only, and it cannot create or change records.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-24 and again on 2026-09-28 on their own pricing page) Four tiers, per user per month: Starter $49, Professional $69, Enterprise $99 and Unlimited $149. Only Unlimited carries a two-user minimum. We had that minimum down as applying to every tier; MRPeasy's partnerships team wrote on 24 August 2026 that it applies to Unlimited alone, and their pricing page prints minimum 2 users under that one plan and nowhere else. Those four rates are what you pay month to month. Pay for a year and one month is free, which the vendor works out as effective rates of Starter $44.92, Professional $63.25, Enterprise $90.75 and Unlimited $136.58; the monthly and annual toggle did not change a single figure on the page when we clicked it in either direction, so those four are the vendor's arithmetic and not our own reading. Mind the currency, because it is not a conversion: the same pricing page served our European browser 39, 59, 79 and 125 euro per user per month on 24 August 2026, with the user bundle at 69 euro, which is about a fifth under the dollar list. Check what your own checkout quotes before you budget. We previously wrote that all plans include unlimited orders and items. The redesigned pricing page no longer says so, and for items the terms say otherwise: active records are capped per edition, with SKUs at 1,000 on Starter, 3,000 on Professional, 7,000 on Enterprise and no built-in cap on Unlimited, and a customer order at 50, 100 and 200 lines. The scaling rule is unusual and worth understanding. The first 10 users pay the tier rate, and from the 11th user you add flat $79 bundles of 10 users. So 11 to 20 users is the base price plus $79, 21 to 30 is plus $158, 31 to 40 plus $237, and so on. Expert support is a separate purchase: one hour a month at $199 billed quarterly ($229 for a single month), two hours at $299 ($349 single) and four hours at $499 ($579 single), with training at $150 an hour.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 29 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two made-up items from a CSV without stock, exported the item list and a backup, and opened the payment page without entering a card.
findings: The trial ran for 15 days ('ends on 13.11.2026'), on the Starter plan. The second 15 days are three rewards of 5 days each, for watching a video, following on LinkedIn and adding a second user who performs 5 actions. They are not automatic.
Before an import MRPeasy recommends downloading a backup, and does it in one click (an .mrp file).

The item import recognised part number, description and selling price by itself. It has no field for notes, tags, dates or custom fields; custom fields are a Professional-plan feature, which the Starter trial does not include.
Two items were imported with zero stock. The CSV export (semicolons) kept part numbers, names with accents and selling prices; the part number is the only key, with no internal ID.
The payment page asks for a card or PayPal but shows no amount, plan or tax. The account page lists 'Next invoice € 39.00' for Starter, monthly, one user.
Users get a permission grid per module (read, create, update, delete), all off by default, rather than named roles. We found no API setting among the integrations in the time we had.
not_tested: Production planning, BOMs and stock movements
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
